scope: Original educational practice; not a validated treatment protocol.
title: Join a familiar activity
revisit: Offer the same familiar activity. Notice whether she wants to join, watch or stop.

steps.do: Bring something she enjoys and sit nearby.
steps.accept: She can watch, join or move away.

steps.do: Follow her interest; describe one thing.
steps.accept: A movement, gesture, look, picture or word may carry meaning.

steps.do: Pause and respond without testing.
steps.accept: No speech or eye contact is required.

scope: Original educational practice; not a validated treatment protocol.
title: Offer two real choices
revisit: Offer the same two available items. Accept either, neither or a change of mind.

steps.do: Put two familiar, available items within comfortable reach.
steps.accept: Choose suitable items for this child; neither is a choice too.

steps.do: Give her quiet time to show her preference.
steps.accept: If her meaning is unclear, show the choices again without pressure.

steps.do: Offer what she indicates.
steps.accept: Do not require a word or screen tap before giving the item.

scope: Original educational practice; not a validated treatment protocol.
title: Show “help” in an everyday moment
revisit: During a familiar activity, show how to ask for help. Help without requiring a response.

steps.do: Join an activity she already likes. Keep the help picture available.
steps.accept: Do not create a problem or take something away to force a request.

steps.do: If help is needed, point to the help picture yourself.
steps.accept: A gesture or movement can also ask for help.

steps.do: Offer help and notice whether it is welcome.
steps.accept: Accept refusal. For an urgent safety need, act without waiting for communication.

scope: Original educational practice; not a validated treatment protocol.
title: Respect “no” and “stop”
revisit: Offer an optional activity. Respond to refusal without asking her to use a particular word.

steps.do: Offer an optional activity and keep “no” and “stop” pictures nearby.
steps.accept: Turning away or moving an item away may mean no; check gently if unsure.

steps.do: Model “no” yourself while pointing to its picture.
steps.accept: She does not have to imitate you.

steps.do: Stop the optional activity when she declines.
steps.accept: Refusal is communication, not a failed lesson.

scope: Original educational practice; not a validated treatment protocol.
title: Ask for a break
revisit: Show the break picture during an optional activity and offer rest.

steps.do: Make a comfortable place to rest available.
steps.accept: She may prefer a different comfortable place.

steps.do: Point to the break picture and pause together.
steps.accept: Rest never depends on using the picture.

steps.do: Let her choose whether to return or finish.
steps.accept: Notice her comfort. Ending early is okay.

scope: Original educational practice; not a validated treatment protocol.
title: Use pictures during a familiar routine
revisit: Keep a familiar picture available during the same routine. Notice any way she communicates.

steps.do: Choose an ordinary routine, such as having water. Keep water freely available.
steps.accept: Use the real object too; a photograph may not be meaningful yet.

steps.do: Point to the matching picture while naming it once.
steps.accept: No copying, naming test or tap is needed.

steps.do: Respond to her communication during the routine.
steps.accept: Do not infer understanding just from a tap; observe the whole interaction.

scope: Original educational practice; not a validated treatment protocol.
title: Repeat a favorite and reflect
revisit: Return to the activity she enjoyed most. Notice what support helped.

steps.do: Offer two activities from this week. Let her choose, or decline.
steps.accept: Choose familiar, age-respectful activities.

steps.do: Use the pictures, gestures or words that helped before.
steps.say: Use one familiar phrase from that activity.
steps.accept: Give the support she needs; independence is not a requirement.

steps.do: Finish comfortably and reflect on what helped.
steps.accept: A week of activities cannot establish mastery or an autism level.
